subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 10, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 10, 2026

Development continues at a steady pace across the AcreetionOS ecosystem with important progress on both the main distribution and related projects. Natalie and Darren have been refining the CI/CD pipelines to improve build reliability and speed. The team is preparing for what will be a significant update to the package management system to enhance repository sovereignty for users.

Recent commits show focused work on the acreetionos-code.github.io repository where newsletter generation and archive maintenance are being automated. The intelligence sync commits from the past two days indicate we're building better integration between documentation, news, and community content. These improvements will help streamline how we share updates with our growing user base.

The acreetionos-immutable project saw critical fixes to the release workflow configuration, ensuring smoother automated builds. Additionally, the AcreetionOS-Xlibre branch received an important addition with firefox-ublock-origin being included in the build configuration. These changes reflect our ongoing commitment to providing privacy-focused browsing capabilities out of the box.

On the security front, the community shared valuable information about weekly security updates affecting various Linux distributions including patches for expat, glib2, and other critical packages. Users are encouraged to keep their systems updated through the standard package management tools. Staying current with security patches remains essential for all Linux users regardless of distribution.

The LibreOffice Base survey results have been shared within the community, providing insights that may inform how we approach office suite integration in future releases. As always, we continue monitoring broader Linux ecosystem developments that could impact our users and contributors.

Community engagement remains vibrant across our Discord server and social platforms where users share experiences, ask questions, and contribute to discussions about the direction of the project. The collaborative spirit that defines AcreetionOS continues to attract new users and contributors who value privacy, sovereignty, and a solid Arch-based foundation.

For those new to AcreetionOS, today's builds represent continued progress toward our goal of creating a user-friendly yet powerful Linux distribution. The Calamares installer has been receiving attention to ensure first-boot experiences are as smooth as possible for newcomers transitioning from other operating systems.

We've added explicit shellcheck linting to our top-level scripts as part of our ongoing code quality initiatives. This extra layer of validation helps maintain the reliability and security of the automation tools that keep AcreetionOS development running smoothly. Both Natalie and Darren have been actively contributing to these infrastructure improvements behind the scenes.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. Whether you're a developer, a system administrator, or simply someone looking for a privacy-respecting operating system, your interest and contributions help make this project stronger. Remember to download the latest release from acreetionos.org and join the conversation on Discord if you haven't already.
